questions.q: Where do rows with a missing value land by default when you call df.sort_values("amount")?
questions.explain: sort_values places missing values last by default. Use na_position="first" to put them at the top.

questions.q: Which rank method for ties behaves like SQL's DENSE_RANK()?
questions.explain: method="dense" gives tied values the same rank and does not skip numbers afterward: 1, 1, 2, 3.

options: Each status's count as a proportion of the total
questions.explain: normalize=True converts counts to proportions that sum to 1. For our illustrative data, shipped is 0.625.

questions.q: You want the biggest order to receive rank 1. What should you pass to rank()?
questions.explain: rank() is ascending by default, so the smallest value gets rank 1. Pass ascending=False to rank the largest value 1.

questions.q: After orders.sort_values("amount"), the first row has index label 2. What happened to the index?
options: Rows were reordered but each row kept its original label
The index became the amount values
questions.explain: Sorting keeps original labels. Add reset_index(drop=True) if you want a new 0, 1, 2 index.
